templates.one_move_blunder: {played_san} leaves your {hung_piece} on {hung_square} undefended, and after {opp_reply_san} you simply lose it for nothing; better was {best_san}, since {best_purpose}. Before you commit a move, check what your opponent can capture and count the trade first.
templates.walked_into_tactic: {front}; instead {best_san} was stronger because {best_purpose}, whereas {played_san} hands material away. Before any quiet move, check that it doesn't run into a tactic that loses a piece.
templates.missed_free_material: {played_san} isn't a blunder, but {best_san} {win}, so you left material on the board. When an enemy piece sits undefended, take it before making a quiet developing move.
templates.missed_mate: Instead of {played_san}, {best_san} was far stronger, throwing a forcing move at the exposed king and keeping the attack rolling. Always look hard at your checks and forcing moves before settling for a quieter line.
templates.allowed_mate: {played_san} lets your opponent force mate, so play {best_san} instead to shore up your king's safety. Before every move, ask what checks and captures your opponent gets.
templates.opening_knowledge: Your {played_san} brings the queen out too early, so Black can attack it and force a retreat while gaining development. Play {best_san} instead—it develops with purpose, fights for the center, and keeps your queen safe; develop your pieces before chasing with the queen.

good_move_templates.develop: Nice move. You bring your {piece} out with {move}, and now it can help your other pieces. Getting your pieces out early like this is a good habit. Lesson: bring your pieces out fast so they can help you, and keep your king safe.
good_move_templates.pawn: You moved your {piece} with {move}. This helps guard your other pieces and opens a path so more of your friends can come out and join the game. Lesson: in the start, put a pawn in the middle and let your pieces come out to play.
good_move_templates.capture: {move} wins free material — when an enemy piece sits undefended and it is safe to take, take it.
good_move_templates.other: Good move. You moved your {piece} to a calm, safe spot with {move}. From here it can do more later. Lesson: when the game is quiet, put each piece on a safe square where it can help you.
good_move_templates.castle: You played {move} to put your {piece} in a safe spot. Good job, that is a smart move. Now bring your other pieces into the game and keep watching over your king. Lesson: make your king safe early so you can play with a calm mind.
good_move_templates.centralize: Nice move. Your {piece} comes out to a good, safe spot where it can do more. Sometimes a different move like another piece coming out or a pawn push is a tiny bit better, but {move} is totally fine, so do not worry. Lesson: bring your pieces out early to good squares so they can help you.
good_move_templates.queen_safety: You played {move} to bring your {piece} back to a safe spot. That keeps it safe, but it does not do much. Lesson: keep your {piece} safe, but try to make every move do a real job.
good_move_templates.space: You pushed your {piece} with {move} and took a little space on the side. That can be okay, but first try to get your other pieces out and your king safe, then push side pawns later. Lesson: bring your pieces out and make your king safe before you push side pawns.
good_move_templates.luft: Your move {move} pushes your {piece} to make a little air for your king. This can be a fine and safe move, but first make sure your king is safe and you are not wasting a turn. Lesson, a small pawn push by your king can give it room, but keep your king safe before you push pawns next to it.
good_move_templates.rook_activity: You moved your {piece} to {move}. From here your {piece} is active and eyes a target, which is good. Lesson: keep your {piece} busy and pointing at something useful.
good_move_templates.rook_open_file: Nice move. Your {piece} goes to {move}. Now it stands on an open file with no pawns in the way, so it can see far and do real work. Lesson: put your {piece}s on open lines where they can reach far and stay busy.

opp_move_templates.develop: Your opponent brought their {piece} out into the game with {move}. This is a normal, safe move that gets their pieces ready, so look at what it now points to and keep your own king safe. Lesson: bring your pieces out early so they can help you.
opp_move_templates.pawn: Your opponent moved a {piece} with {move}. See what it touches or blocks, then bring your own pieces out and keep your king safe. Lesson: when your opponent pushes a pawn, stay calm and get your pieces ready to play.
opp_move_templates.other: Your opponent moved their {piece} with {move}. This is a quiet, calm move and does not really hit anything of yours, so do not worry. Now it is your turn, so pick a safe, useful move and keep your own king safe too. Lesson: when your opponent makes a quiet move, stay calm and find a smart plan of your own.
opp_move_templates.castle: Your opponent played {move} to put their king in a safe spot. Their {piece} is now tucked away in the corner, so it is harder for you to attack it. Make a plan of your own and keep playing calmly. The lesson is simple: make your own king safe early too.
opp_move_templates.centralize: Your opponent moved their {piece} with {move} to a strong spot in the middle. Look right away to see if you can just take it for nothing or push it away with a smaller piece. Lesson: when a piece comes near, first check if you can take it or chase it off.
opp_move_templates.queen_safety: Your opponent moved the {piece} with {move}. Now it is your turn, so look for the safest and best move you can make. Lesson, when your opponent moves a piece, ask what it now does and keep your own pieces safe.
opp_move_templates.space: Your opponent just played {move}, pushing a pawn to take more room on the board. This gives their {piece} more space, so be ready and do not let them push you back. Keep playing your own plan and bring your pieces to good, safe squares. Lesson: when the other side gains space, stay calm and make your own pieces strong.
opp_move_templates.luft: Your opponent played {move}. This makes a little safe spot for the king and stops back row tricks, but it is a slow move that does not help much. You can keep on with your own plan, and watch if that {piece} pokes one of your pieces and asks it to move. Lesson: a small, quiet pawn move is slow, so use your turn to bring a piece out instead.
opp_move_templates.rook_activity: Your opponent moved their {piece} with {move}. Now it is active and eyes a target on your side. Look at what it points to, and keep that piece and your king safe. Lesson: when your opponent's rook gets active, see what it aims at and guard it.
opp_move_templates.rook_open_file: Your opponent played {move} and put the {piece} on an open line. Now it can look far down that line at your pieces, so check what it is aiming at. Keep your pieces safe and watch your king. Lesson: when a {piece} moves to an open line, look at what it attacks before you move.
